title: A Prayer of the Godly
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Despair
subpoints: The perception that the godly are disappearing from society
The overwhelming presence of wickedness and false speech
The contrast between external circumstances and internal faith

outline.title: The Response of the Godly: Turning to God
subpoints: Praying 'Help, Lord' as the primary response to crisis
Contrast with Elijah’s reaction to persecution and isolation
Recognizing God as the only source of true help and refuge

outline.title: The Evidence of Wickedness: Corrupt Speech
subpoints: Flattering lips and double-hearted speech as markers of the wicked
The perversion of truth in society
The silence of the godly in the face of cultural lies

outline.title: The Path to Joy: Right Thinking and Acting
subpoints: Overcoming depression not by changing circumstances, but by changing perspective
Trusting in God’s promises and the purity of His Word
Finding peace through a biblically informed view of the world

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores Psalm 12, focusing on the experience of the godly person living in a world characterized by wickedness and false speech. The psalm begins with a cry for help, reflecting the despair that arises when the faithful seem to disappear and society is dominated by flattering lips and double hearts. The pastor highlights that this despair is not necessarily due to a literal absence of believers, but rather the overwhelming noise of cultural lies and the silence of the godly who fail to stand for righteousness.

The message contrasts the psalmist’s response with that of the prophet Elijah. While Elijah retreated into self-pity and isolation when facing Jezebel’s threat, the psalmist turns directly to God, acknowledging Him as the only source of help and refuge. This distinction illustrates the difference between a faith tethered to external circumstances and a faith rooted in the character and promises of God.

The sermon concludes by emphasizing that true joy and peace are not dependent on the resolution of external problems, but on a biblically informed worldview. By trusting in the purity of God’s Word and acting in accordance with His truth, the godly can overcome depression and despair. The pastor encourages believers to stop waiting for circumstances to change before finding peace, and instead to find their stability in God’s unchanging nature and His promise to preserve the faithful.
